    Integral weights on thin categories (Proposition 7.2, first part) #

    That paper (prop:integral-ray-weights): "For a finite directed thin representation-finite category T […] let U(T) be the abelian group generated by symbols [r] for the nonidentity morphism lines r of T, with relations [rr'] = [r] + [r'] whenever rr' ≠ 0. For a source s, put T' = T ∖ {s} and form the category R of Lemma 4.11 […] Lemma 4.9 gives object values u_y ∈ U(T'), normalized to zero at one root y_D in each connected component D of R. The new nonzero-product relations are exactly [sy] + [b_yz] = [sz]. They have the universal solutions [sy] = c_D + u_y. […] Thus U(T) ≅ U(T') ⊕ ℤ^{π₀(R)}, preserving the old generators. The sink assertion follows by opposites. […] a nonzero element of the free group U(L) has a nonzero integer coordinate m, detected by a character to k* […] But Lemma 4.13 says that every such character is an object ratio".

    Formalization. Weights are recorded additively (IsAddWeight), a k*-weight being an Additive kˣ-valued one. The induction over sources and sinks proves the separation property Sep T: an integer combination of lines killed by every k*-weight is killed by every weight with values in any abelian group. This is the form in which the freeness of U(T) and of its split extensions is used for the detection by characters: the universal solutions [sy] = c_D + u_y appear as the decomposition ev_insert_source, the summand ℤ^{π₀(R)} as the free constants c_D (extW), and the character detecting a nonzero coordinate as exists_zpow_ne_one. Combined with Lemma 4.13 this gives Proposition 7.2(2) (addWeight_eq_diff).

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.
